key_highlights: NAB cutting 2,500 jobs signals major structural shift in Australian banking sector, with fears of industry-wide contagion
ASX falls despite AI-driven Wall Street rebound, with NAB and BHP leading declines
Steelworks closures in Whyalla compound materials sector weakness
Junior miners reporting strong gold, rare earths and manganese discoveries across WA, NT and West Africa
Iron ore sentiment deteriorating as Vale signals supply-side concerns and China growth outlook dims
Perth property market enters bust phase; new home sales dropping — housing sector headwinds intensifying
Oil prices surging, benefiting Australian energy producers
China export boom flagged as structural risk, with car flood and trade dynamics threatening commodity demand

sectors.trend: Deeply negative. NAB axing 2,500 jobs is the most market-moving domestic headline. Cost-cutting signals margin pressure, AI displacement of white-collar roles, and management concern about forward revenue. Contagion risk to CBA, ANZ, WBC is elevated.
sectors.implications: Bank sector likely to underperform near-term. Dividend sustainability in focus. Investors should reassess Big Four exposure. AI-driven restructuring is a secular headwind to employment costs but near-term reputational and morale risk is high.

sectors.trend: Negative to neutral. Iron ore sentiment weakening as Vale flags concerns, China growth apathy grows, and Whyalla steelworks job losses confirm domestic steel demand stress. BHP declining on ASX today.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX and RIO.AX face near-term price pressure. FMG.AX most exposed to iron ore spot moves. Whyalla closure risk is a negative read-through for BlueScope Steel (BSL.AX).

sectors.trend: Positive. Multiple junior explorers reporting high-grade gold hits (WA, West Africa, NT), a monster $2.7B rare earths valuation in WA, manganese jackpot in Pilbara, and Mongolian gas discovery. Junior mining pipeline is active.
sectors.implications: Gold explorers (Aurum, Great Southern, Kaiser) and rare earths plays (Critica) are key watchlist names. Broader gold sector supported. Critical minerals theme remains strong amid global supply chain diversification push.

sectors.trend: Bullish. Oil is described as 'relentless' and 'rocketing', suggesting sustained upward price momentum. Gas discovery in Mongolia adds longer-dated optionality. Court scrutiny of data centre gas plants introduces regulatory risk for gas infrastructure.
sectors.implications: Woodside (WDS.AX), Santos (STO.AX) and Beach Energy (BPT.AX) are direct beneficiaries of oil/gas price strength. Regulatory overhang from cumulative emissions scrutiny warrants monitoring for LNG project approvals.

sectors.trend: Negative. Perth leading a national house price bust. New home sales dropping fast. Sydney supply-demand mismatch flagged. These signals point to prolonged housing correction.
sectors.implications: Residential-exposed REITs and developers under pressure. Stockland (SGP.AX), Mirvac (MGR.AX) most at risk. Commercial REITs less directly impacted. Banks face rising mortgage stress risk if correction deepens.

sectors.trend: Mildly negative. Banana shortage hitting supermarket shelves adds food inflation pressure. Cost-of-living stress, combined with mass layoffs, is a headwind for discretionary spending.
sectors.implications: Woolworths (WOW.AX) and Coles (COL.AX) face input cost pressure from produce shortages. Consumer sentiment fragile as job cuts accumulate.

sectors.trend: Mixed. Wall Street AI rebound did not translate to ASX gains. AI alarm bells ringing louder on Wall Street suggests valuation concerns. AI is simultaneously driving NAB job cuts — a double-edged theme.
sectors.implications: ASX tech sector (WTC.AX, XRO.AX) may lag US peers if AI enthusiasm wanes. AI adoption is accelerating bank automation but creating labour market disruption domestically.

sectors.trend: Neutral to negative. Health system described as in 'perpetual crisis' with calls for a public inquiry. Systemic underfunding could create regulatory and policy headwinds.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, Ramsay Health Care (RHC.AX) — watch for policy shifts in public vs private healthcare funding. Inquiry could accelerate reform but near-term uncertainty persists.

key_themes: Bank sector restructuring: NAB job cuts signal AI-driven displacement and margin compression across the Big Four
Iron ore / bulk commodity demand risk from China slowdown and Vale supply signals
Junior gold and critical minerals explorer activity surging in WA and NT
Oil price strength benefiting Australian energy producers
Housing market correction accelerating — Perth leading nationally
AI adoption creating labour market disruption, with recession fears rising
China structural risks: export surplus, car flood, subdued domestic growth
Regulatory risk escalating in energy (gas emissions), coal (High Court ruling), and education

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Banking sector job cuts and AI displacement — systemic labour market shock
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce Big Four bank exposure; monitor CBA.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX for follow-on announcements. Favour cost-efficient fintechs.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Iron ore price deterioration driven by China growth apathy and Vale supply signals
risk_assessment.mitigation: Trim FMG.AX (highest iron ore leverage). Maintain diversified BHP.AX and RIO.AX as partial hedge via copper/potash exposure.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Residential property correction deepening — mortgage stress and bank loan quality risk
risk_assessment.mitigation: Avoid residential developer stocks (SGP.AX, MGR.AX). Monitor bank NPL trends in quarterly updates.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: AI valuation correction on Wall Street spilling into ASX tech and growth stocks
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce growth/tech overweights. Rotate into value and defensive sectors (utilities, infrastructure, consumer staples).

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Energy regulatory risk: court scrutiny of gas plant emissions, High Court coal ruling
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor legal proceedings for gas infrastructure exposure. Woodside and Santos to be watched on approvals pipeline.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: China export surplus becoming geopolitical flashpoint — trade war escalation risk
risk_assessment.mitigation: Diversify commodity exposure beyond China-dependent iron ore. Favour gold, rare earths, LNG with diversified buyer base.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Recession risk rising as corporate layoffs accumulate
risk_assessment.mitigation: Increase defensive allocation (consumer staples, healthcare, infrastructure). Watch RBA rate decision signals closely.

opportunities.recommendation: Accumulate gold explorers and producers on continued high-grade discovery newsflow
opportunities.rationale: Multiple WA and NT gold hits signal active exploration cycle. Gold typically outperforms in risk-off environments and benefits from AUD weakness.

opportunities.recommendation: Selective exposure to rare earths and critical minerals plays in WA and NT
opportunities.rationale: Critica's $2.7B WA rare earths valuation and 8km NT rare earths extension confirm major resource potential. Critical minerals remain strategically supported by government policy.

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight oil and gas producers as oil prices surge
opportunities.rationale: Oil described as 'relentless' and 'rocketing' — direct earnings uplift for Australian LNG and oil producers. AUD weakness amplifies USD-denominated commodity revenue.

opportunities.recommendation: Monitor Accelerate Resources following Pilbara manganese jackpot
opportunities.rationale: 59.6% Mn grades in Pilbara are exceptionally high. Manganese is a critical battery and steel input with tightening supply.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce exposure to NAB and monitor Big Four banks for contagion
defensive_moves.rationale: 2,500 NAB job cuts signal deep structural cost pressure. AI-led restructuring will compress revenue per employee ratios and may trigger further cuts at CBA, ANZ, WBC.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore-leveraged positions, especially FMG.AX
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore sentiment souring on Vale supply fears and China growth indifference. FMG has highest pure-play iron ore exposure of the majors.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce residential property developer and REIT exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Perth leading a national house price bust, new home sales dropping. Developers and residential REITs face valuation and earnings downside.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Add defensives — consumer staples and healthcare — to buffer recessionary risk
defensive_moves.rationale: Rising corporate layoffs and recession language from analysts warrant defensive rotation. Staples and healthcare offer earnings resilience.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Consider index put protection on ^AXJO given multiple concurrent headwinds
defensive_moves.rationale: Simultaneous bank layoffs, iron ore weakness, housing bust, AI valuation risk, and China growth concerns create compounding downside risk to the broader index.

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish. The ASX faces concurrent headwinds: NAB job cuts triggering sector-wide bank re-rating, iron ore weakness, a deepening housing correction, and Wall Street AI uncertainty not translating into domestic gains. Expect range-bound to declining ASX 200 in the 1-3 month window. Key support levels at ^AXJO will be tested. Oil and gold sectors are the primary bright spots.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously neutral with selective opportunity. Critical minerals and gold remain structurally supported by energy transition and geopolitical diversification themes. If RBA pivots to rate cuts in response to rising unemployment and recession signals, rate-sensitive sectors (REITs, utilities) could re-rate positively over 6-12 months. Banking sector recovery depends on pace of AI integration and macro stabilisation. China structural risks (car export flood, low domestic growth) remain a persistent drag on bulk commodity earnings.
